relevant_entries.body:
## PIPELINE ROADMAP APPEND — Bing's cold/warm-start distinction (2026-11-03)

Source: Mark pasted a proposal attributed to Bing; Meraki records an attributed summary, not a direct Bing GitHub post. [Contribution and design response](https://github.com/MarkDude-design/ALLurbaseRnotbelong2us/blob/fe35e0fe0c5f7b6501829362f6027344f5fb0ebc/docs/pipeline-contributions/BING_COLD_WARM_START_2026_11_03.md), in unmerged PR #17.

Cold start = project/role/current-state orientation. Warm start = changes since the returning seat's last verified receipt. The existing decision ledger preserves recorded reasons, evidence and superseded decisions; an optional narrative is a source-linked view, not another authority. The pasted sample names, decisions, roles and successes are illustrative, not verified team state.

Roadmap refinement: apply both cold and warm entry points across A/B/C rather than adding a fourth framework. Warm views should have explicit from/to source horizons; a missing cursor or source gap needs bounded cold reconciliation. Expiring a sticky-note display must not erase unread work or its source decisions.

Next proposed test: last-read receipt + resolved blocker + newly pending action + unrelated fragment + duplicate delivery; check material delta coverage, preserved project focus and missing-cursor fallback. NOT RUN. Earlier 10/10 three-reader results remain a cold-start synthetic trial only.

Three documentation changes fetched back exactly at fe35e0fe0c5f7b6501829362f6027344f5fb0ebc. Z's desk and the live QC next action are unchanged. No associated code needed yet; no execution, queue entry, spending, timer or merge added by this note.

## BEST PRACTICES — Meraki-owned guide and saved reader markers (2026-11-03)

Mark assigned Meraki a reusable best-practices guide to complement Z's style guide. [Guide](https://github.com/MarkDude-design/ALLurbaseRnotbelong2us/blob/8b25f260ab22251fa2e7b4b411f8c31da52d9ea9/docs/TEAM_BEST_PRACTICES.md) · [pipeline map](https://github.com/MarkDude-design/ALLurbaseRnotbelong2us/blob/8b25f260ab22251fa2e7b4b411f8c31da52d9ea9/docs/TEAM_PIPELINE_MAP.md) · [saved per-stream reader horizons](https://github.com/MarkDude-design/ALLurbaseRnotbelong2us/blob/8b25f260ab22251fa2e7b4b411f8c31da52d9ea9/docs/pipeline-state/meraki.json). Readable in PR #17, still unmerged.

The intended everyday request is **warm start the pipeline**; the agent retrieves its own markers instead of asking Mark for a number. Exact IDs remain an optional debugging override. Markers advance only after a successful read, stay separate by source thread/seat, and missing horizons need bounded cold reconciliation. Saved markers exist; automatic fresh-thread loading and synchronization are not claimed.

Observed real test: Mark's greeting was on PR #17 comment 6610423448, not index #16. The direct comment lookup found the correct thread; no later comments existed at the read horizon. Greeting received without inventing a task or approval. This demonstrates referenced note retrieval, not a full native cold start.

The guide also covers focused worker projects with a side-note hotpad, direct/relayed/hosted delivery, exact attribution, recorded decision reasons, proportionate checks and precise test claims. Z's desk, queue and style ownership remain unchanged.

Portability: a separate dated recovery snapshot has been saved outside GitHub. It carries project state, source revision, reader horizons and scope; it is not automatically synchronized. Official OpenAI Pages documentation supports shared reference content and reusable prompts, but no selected Page or Page-editing tool was available here, so Canvas recovery is untested. Next optional portability test: a new reader recovers from the snapshot or an explicitly supplied Page, then reconciles live sources when available.

Four repository files fetched back exactly at 8b25f260ab22251fa2e7b4b411f8c31da52d9ea9. No new deployment, paid call, timer or merge. Meraki owns guide maintenance; QC's real hotpad round trip remains the next integration action.

relevant_entries.body:
## PRIORITY CLARIFICATION — Meraki cold start HIGH; broader tooling MEDIUM (2026-11-03)

This corrects the blanket medium-priority entry at 6611047266. Mark explicitly clarified that Meraki's cold-start path is **HIGH priority / active**. The wider QC/Bing/Q integration, cloud options and desk fine-tuning stay **MEDIUM / prepared**.

Meraki selects candidate B: a short evidence-first entry with a portable recovery snapshot. [Usable cold-start entry](https://github.com/MarkDude-design/ALLurbaseRnotbelong2us/blob/26963e66a95540c5895d99e8ab44fc08f166c370/docs/COLD_START.md). The task is to use the candidate, observe several actual return episodes and refine from evidence; one fixture pass is insufficient to judge reliability. A fresh-context reader may provide a clearly labeled surrogate test, not proof that the continuing Meraki thread restarted.

Current action: align the saved snapshot with this priority, run one bounded operational snapshot/source reconciliation, preserve its result and record later natural returns separately. No scheduler created; Z's desk is not reassigned. Four repository files fetched back exactly at 26963e66a95540c5895d99e8ab44fc08f166c370. Prepared files remain in unmerged PR #17.
